content: The Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) conducted between 2010 and 2012 was published in Maturitas in 2017, highlighting findings on health and nutrition trends in Korea. Kikafunda et al. (1998) identified risk factors for early childhood malnutrition in Uganda, as reported in Pediatrics. Kim et al. (2015) found an association between breastfeeding and postmenopausal bone loss, based on data from the KNHANES, published in the Korean Journal of Family Medicine. Another study by Kim and Choi (2020) explored the relationship between breastfeeding and cognitive function in children from early childhood to school age, as detailed in the International Breastfeeding Journal. Kondolot et al. (2017) examined risk factors for overweight and obesity in children aged 2-6 years, as published in the Journal of Pediatric Endocrinology and Metabolism. Krenz-Niedbała et al. (2015) investigated whether the relationship between breastfeeding and childhood risks of asthma and obesity is mediated by infant antibiotic treatment, as reported in Breastfeeding Medicine. Kvale and Heuch (1987) explored the relationship between lactation and breast cancer risk in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health. Lee et al. (2005) examined whether long-term lactation protects premenopausal women against hypertension risk in a Korean cohort study, published in Preventive Medicine. Lee et al. (2016) studied the effect of breastfeeding duration on cognitive development in infants over a three-year follow-up, as reported in the Journal of Korean Medical Science. Li et al. (2020) identified a U-shaped association between breastfeeding duration and cognitive impairment in Chinese postmenopausal women, published in Scientific Reports. Liese et al. (2001) reported an inverse association between breastfeeding and overweight in 9-10-year-old children in Germany, as published in the International Journal of Obesity. Lima et al. (2019) examined the relationship between breastfeeding and maternal cardiovascular risk factors in the 1982 Pelotas Birth Cohort, published in Scientific Reports. Victora et al. (2015) studied the association between breastfeeding and intelligence, educational attainment, and income at 30 years of age in a Brazilian cohort, as reported in The Lancet Global Health. Linhares et al. (2015) explored the impact of breastfeeding on body composition and growth in children, as published in PLOS ONE. London et al. (1990) investigated lactation and breast cancer risk in a cohort of U.S. women, as reported in the American Journal of Epidemiology. Lossius et al. (2018) conducted a prospective cohort study on breastfeeding and the risk of childhood asthma, published in The Journal of Pediatrics. Luo et al. (2019) examined the associations between parity, breastfeeding, and maternal type 2 diabetes risk among postmenopausal women, as reported in Obstetrics & Gynecology. Lupton et al. Maguire et al. (2013) investigated the association between breastfeeding duration and iron deficiency in children, as reported in Pediatrics. Martin et al. (2002) explored the relationship between breastfeeding and growth in the Boyd-Orr cohort study, published in Archives of Disease in Childhood: Fetal and Neonatal Edition. Michels et al. (1996) conducted a prospective assessment of breastfeeding and breast cancer incidence among nearly 90,000 women, as reported in The Lancet. Miyake et al. (2007) studied allergic disorders associated with breastfeeding in Japan, as published in Pediatric Allergy and Immunology. Muniz et al. (2015) analyzed breastfeeding and bone mass at ages 18 and 30 in the Pelotas cohorts, as reported in PLOS ONE. Mwakayoka et al. (2017) examined dental caries and associated factors in children aged 2-4 years in Tanzania, published in the Journal of Dentistry Shiraz Medical Sciences. Nam et al. (2019) explored the associations between breastfeeding and type 2 diabetes mellitus and glycemic control in parous women, as reported in the Diabetes & Metabolism Journal. Nambiar et al. (2013) investigated the influence of breastfeeding on abdominal adiposity in young children, as published in Nutrition & Dietetics. Natland et al. (2012) studied lactation and cardiovascular risk factors in mothers in the HUNT study, published in the International Breastfeeding Journal. Neutzling et al. (2009) examined infant feeding and obesity at 11 years in a prospective birth cohort study, as reported in the International Journal of Pediatric Obesity. Nguyen et al. (2019) explored breastfeeding and cardiovascular disease hospitalization and mortality in parous women, as published in the Journal of the American Heart Association. Nirunsittirat et al. (2016) studied breastfeeding duration and childhood caries in a cohort study, published in Caries Research. Novaes et al. (2012) examined the association between prolonged breastfeeding and early childhood caries, as reported in Community Dentistry and Oral Epidemiology. Obihara et al. (2005) investigated the association of prolonged breastfeeding and allergic disease in poor urban children, as published in the European Respiratory Journal. Oddy et al. (2010) studied the long-term effects of breastfeeding on child and adolescent mental health in a pregnancy cohort study, published in The Journal of Pediatrics. Okyay et al. (2013) identified prolonged breastfeeding as an independent risk factor for postmenopausal osteoporosis, as reported in Maturitas. Olatosi et al. (2014) examined the prevalence of early childhood caries and its associated risk factors among preschool children in Nigeria, published in the Nigerian Journal of Clinical Practice.
